resources.string: Your last Geode style, reacting to whatever the app is playing and drifting gently when it is not.
Geode — now playing in other apps
Shown while Geode is reading the audio another app is playing.
Geode is reading the audio playing on this device.
Shown while Geode is rendering a video, so the render is not interrupted.
Geode reacts to music with light, and the visuals are intense — bright, fast and full-screen.

The flash rate is limited in the engine, by design. Nothing on screen can flash more than three times a second, no preset or imported file can raise that, and the video you export is held to the same limit as the screen you saw. There is no setting for this and nothing to switch off.
Pick your media library, a folder, or both. Scanning starts straight away and everything stays usable while it runs.
This sets where the app opens. You can change it later in Settings.
Opens on the player. Studio stays out of the way.
Opens in Studio, with your projects and render queue to hand.
Opens on the player, with Studio one tap away.
Edits are stored in the app only — audio files are not modified.
Plays music from your device and renders it. No account, no ads, no analytics — nothing leaves the phone unless you export a video and share it.
Third-party notices could not be loaded.
The last run crashed. Copy the report to share it, then dismiss.\n\n%1$s
%1$s will not be captured — see Settings
Your library, your history, or the room
The visuals are on the connected display. Everything here still controls them — turn this off in Settings › Live input & touch to bring them back.

Drop an .lrc file next to the track — same name, .lrc extension — and it shows up here, timed and following the music. Words written into the file\'s own tags are read too. Nothing is fetched: the app has no network access.
Timed lyrics from %1$s. Tap a line to jump there.
Nothing queued. Playing anything from a list — the library, a shelf on Home, a search result — queues that whole list.
Grant music access to browse everything on this device.
Music access is turned off for Geode, and Android will not ask again from here. Open app settings to turn on Music and audio.
\"%1$s\" is removed. Its tracks stay in the library.
There is already a playlist called \"%1$s\".
No playlists yet. Start one with \"New playlist\" above, save the current queue from the queue panel in Now Playing, or use \"Add to playlist\" in any track\'s ⋮ menu.
Render a visual from Settings › Export video and it lands here, ready to be cut, graded and sent somewhere. Any other video on the phone can be opened with the button above.
\"%1$s\" will be deleted from this device. This cannot be undone.
Android would not let Geode delete that file.
A look writes these four and then gets out of the way — every one stays an ordinary slider afterwards, the same way the live-input profiles work.
Reframing crops rather than pillarboxes — turning 16:9 into 9:16 means losing the sides, and black bars are the one result nobody wants from that.
Drawn into the frame after everything else, so it is not graded or cropped with the picture. Leave it empty for none.
Send opens the phone\'s own share sheet — YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, Drive, a message, whatever is installed and signed in. Geode has no network access of its own and never uploads anything itself.
Nothing is changed yet — rendering now would just copy the clip.
Renders a NEW file. The original is never overwritten.
Fade on pause, resume and skip — off

Ramps the volume instead of cutting it. Not a crossfade — one player decodes one track at a time, and a second one would give the analyser two streams to sum — but it removes the hard edges, which is the part you hear.
Pausing after the track playing in %1$s
Play something first — the effects chain attaches to the audio session, and there is no session until audio starts.
This device would not grant an equalizer. What it did grant is below.
Exports land in your Videos library (Movies/Geode), or in a folder you pick at render time — there is no standing export folder to configure. Defaults for quality and size live in the Export tab.
Preset folder: chosen — saves are mirrored there
Presets always save inside the app; a chosen folder gets a mirror copy so your own sorting is visible in any file manager.
No folders yet. Device music appears in the Library on its own; folders you add here are scanned into the import library as well.
The same list as Library › Folders. Rescanning re-walks every folder; tracks already imported keep their analysis.
Analysis results per track, so replaying never re-analyses. Clearing costs nothing but the next analysis pass.
"Beat sensitivity %1$sσ — drag right for LESS sensitive (fewer beat flashes)"
"Minimum gap between beats %1$d ms — never flash faster than %2$d BPM"

Sets Hue shift from the key the analyser found, around the circle of fifths — so a track keeps the same colour every time you play it, and two songs that sound related look related. It moves the ordinary Hue shift slider, so you can always disagree with it; switching this off gives your own value back.

Plays nothing and drives the visuals from what the phone hears — a room, an instrument, a speaker across the street. Playback pauses while it is on, because the analyzer has one input and a track plus the room would just blur together. Audio is analysed live and never recorded, saved or sent anywhere.
Microphone access is off for Geode. Turn it on in Android Settings › Apps › Geode › Permissions to use live input.
The microphone could not be opened — another app may be using it.
Tune for what the phone is hearing
Each sets the beat threshold, the reactivity envelope and the band balance together — they are one decision, and they live on three different screens. Every value stays an ordinary slider afterwards.
Needs Android 10 or newer — the API that lets one app read another app\'s audio arrived with it. Live input (the microphone) works on every version and can hear the same speaker.

Drives the visuals from whatever is already playing on this device — a streaming app, a video, a game — instead of from a file in your library. Android asks for capture permission first, and shows a notification the whole time it is running. Audio is analysed live and never recorded, saved or sent anywhere.
Listening. Start something playing in any app.

Geode can also show WHAT the other app is playing — the track and artist, on the visualizer. That reads the media session, which Android gates behind notification access. Optional: the visuals work on the sound alone.

%1$s does not allow other apps to capture its audio. Android honours that, and there is no setting on either side that changes it — the capture is running and being handed digital silence. Most other apps (YouTube, podcast players, games) do allow it and work here.
The microphone still hears your speaker. It picks up the room with it, so it is a rougher signal — but it reacts to %1$s.
This device is older than Android 10, which introduced audio capture between apps.
Microphone access is off for Geode. Android requires it for audio capture of any kind — turn it on in Android Settings › Apps › Geode › Permissions.
Capture permission was not given. Nothing is being read.
The device would not open an audio capture at any format — another app may be holding it.

Loop-safe trims the end of the render to a bar boundary so the clip repeats cleanly when a platform autoplays it. It needs a detected tempo, so a track that has not been analysed falls back to full length for that render.
Starts from the defaults above; each render can change them for one video. The destination — your Videos library or a folder you pick — is chosen at render time, per export.
You can leave Geode — the render keeps going and finishes in the background.
Drag to pick at least %1$d second of the track. Anything shorter renders the whole thing instead.
Renders %1$s–%2$s (%3$s). The clip starts at 0:00 in the file, and the visuals are the ones from that part of the track.

Loop-safe cuts on a bar boundary (%1$s BPM, %2$s s per bar) so the last beat runs into the first — what a short clip needs when a platform autoplays it on repeat. Up to one bar is trimmed from the end.
Loop-safe needs a detected tempo. Analyse the track (Now Playing › Auto) and reopen this dialog.

Renders the take\'s parameter automation — every slider, colour and effect moving as you performed it. A style SWITCH inside the take is not reproduced: the render draws through the style selected now, for its whole length.
4K depends on your device\'s encoder; it falls back automatically if unsupported.
Scales every font in the app, live - including this one.
Pale colors are greyed out on this light theme - they could not be read on its surfaces.
Recolors the writing everywhere; Auto returns to the theme\'s own text colors.
Text-only Visuals menu over the live visuals, so adjustments are visible as you make them.
Smear the visuals with a finger

Drag on the fullscreen visualizer to push the image around: the drag raises the surface ahead of your finger and dips it behind, and whatever is on screen bends through it. On the Water style it stirs the pool itself and paints into it.

Two fingers on the fullscreen visualizer: pinch moves the Zoom slider, twist moves Rotation. They are the same controls the Customize panel shows, so a gesture is saved into presets and takes — and undone by dragging the slider back.
Connected: %1$s. The visuals play there and the phone becomes the control surface — the canvas moves rather than being mirrored, so the big screen shows exactly what the app renders.
Nothing connected. Plug in HDMI or start casting, and the visuals move to that screen while the phone keeps the controls.

Nothing in Geode can flash more than three times a second. Published guidance (WCAG 2.3.1) puts the general limit there, and the clamp sits in the render path itself — it applies to every scene, every preset and every imported file, on screen and in exported video alike. It is not a setting, so there is nothing here to adjust.

Slows movement, shake, drift and rotation. This one is about motion comfort rather than seizures, which is why it is a choice: the flash limit above is not. Applies to exported video as well as the screen.

Set the visualizer as your wallpaper. It uses the style and settings the app was last showing, reacts to whatever Geode is playing, and drifts gently on its own the rest of the time. It draws nothing while another app is in front, so it is not a background battery drain.
Two modes rotate the look on a clock while a track plays. Only one of them runs at a time: starting the visual playlist stops Random, and turning Random on stops the playlist.
Random is off — the visual playlist below has it.
Random is off — the Auto button on the Now Playing screen turns it on.
The settings below shape it whether it is running or not, so a session can be set up before it starts — and they are remembered across restarts.

Waits for a big moment in the music instead of switching the instant the timer is up, so a change lands with the track rather than across it. It still holds a look for at least half the interval, and forces a switch at twice it, so a quiet passage cannot stall the rotation.
Nothing is selected, so Random has nothing to switch to and will leave the visuals alone.
Styles are the built-in looks; saved presets carry their own settings with them.

Rolls both palettes, the blend between them and the hue shift on every switch. It clears a custom palette you made in Customize › Color, because that override outranks the palettes being rolled and the new ones would otherwise never show.
Random is running — turning this on will stop it.
Add looks with the heart button in Visuals › Presets. The playlist needs at least two before it has anywhere to go.
The same timing Random\'s \"strong beat\" uses, applied to the playlist order: the next look still comes next, it just waits for a moment worth arriving on.
Loops your cut, muted — grade, speed and reframe show as they will render. Tap to pause.
Preset \"%1$s\" imported — it is in Visuals › Presets.
That preset link could not be read. It may have been cut short in transit.
None yet — build a gradient above and save it.
